row_liveness.question: Does the dispatcher establish that the row returned by X509V3_EXT_get is live against a concurrent X509V3_EXT_add/_add_alias/_cleanup, and is the reachable set only static rows?
row_liveness.lookup_order: X509V3_EXT_get -> X509V3_EXT_get_nid: the STANDARD_EXTS binary search answers first (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:683-701); the dynamic EXT_LIST is consulted only when that search misses (:719-731), all under the registry read hold.
row_liveness.callbacks_are_private: The 22 boundary functions are module-private `unsafe [extern "C"] fn`s with no #[no_mangle]; the 15 slot callbacks appear only as function-pointer values in crate-owned rows, and the 7 helpers are called only from those rows. None of the 16 printer files references X509V3_EXT_add/_add_list/_add_alias/_cleanup/_get/_get_nid, so a printer cannot re-enter a registry writer from inside the read hold.
row_liveness.static_rows: The 15 slot callbacks are installed only in crate-owned `pub static` method rows reached through STANDARD_EXTS; for a standard NID the dynamic list is never consulted, so those rows are process-lifetime statics that X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release.
row_liveness.dynamic_rows: X509V3_EXT_add (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:613-620) accepts a caller row; X509V3_EXT_add_alias (:788-827) copies a row (including its i2r pointer) into a DYNAMIC allocation and registers it; X509V3_EXT_cleanup (:661-668) swaps EXT_LIST to NULL and pop_free's the list, releasing every DYNAMIC row through ext_list_free (:544-559). A dynamic alias of a standard row therefore carries one of the 22 callbacks and is reachable through the dynamic fallback for its new NID. X509V3_EXT_add_nid does not exist in this crate or in the pinned 3.6.4 authority; the registration entry points are _add, _add_list and _add_alias.
row_liveness.locking: EXT_LIST is guarded by REGISTRY_LOCK, a CRYPTO_RWLOCK created by the REGISTRY_ONCE run-once (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:437-508). Every entry point takes the hold before touching the list: X509V3_EXT_add/_add_list/_add_alias/_cleanup take the write hold; X509V3_EXT_get_nid/_get take the read hold. The authority's lazy OPENSSL_sk_sort moved from the lookup into ext_add_locked (:565-596), so the lookup is read-only. X509V3_EXT_print takes the read hold at src/x509/v3_prn.rs:271-273 and holds it across resolution and every use of the row. The 22 printers do not take the lock themselves.
row_liveness.crate_callers: No non-test code in src/ calls X509V3_EXT_add/_add_list/_add_alias/_cleanup (grep); those entry points are exported ABI, so an external consumer can register a row or run cleanup. The registry lock makes concurrent registration/cleanup memory-safe.
row_liveness.conclusion: Only-static-rows is NOT established: the exported registration/cleanup ABI makes a DYNAMIC alias row (carrying a standard row's i2r) reachable. B49-R10 is CLOSED by the registry read/write hold: a cleanup cannot release a dynamic row while X509V3_EXT_print is resolving or using it. The raw X509V3_EXT_get[_nid] ABI still returns a borrowed row, so an external caller that keeps using that pointer across its own X509V3_EXT_cleanup remains responsible for excluding that call; the crate's dispatcher does not rely on that. The dispositions were not applied and the closure was not run.

hidden_obligations_note: The retained obligations are stated in the fn-level contracts and in B49-R2/R3/R4: the registrar must keep each row's `it` paired with its `i2r`, `out` liveness is the caller's, and exclusive use of the decoded value is the dispatcher's. B49-R10 (row liveness across the call) is no longer a retained caller obligation: X509V3_EXT_print holds the registry read hold across resolution and use, and every writer takes the write hold. None is hidden.
new_unsafe_assumptions_note: Three private unsafe fns: ext_method_item, ext_add_locked and ext_get_nid_locked. ext_method_item's `method` is live because X509V3_EXT_print holds the registry read hold (:271-273); ext_add_locked requires the caller to hold the write hold (X509V3_EXT_add/_add_list/_add_alias do); ext_get_nid_locked requires the read or write hold (X509V3_EXT_get_nid/_get and the writers do). The guard constructors are safe fns whose bodies wrap CRYPTO_THREAD_read_lock/write_lock and CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock with SAFETY comments; the run-once body calls only CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new. No new site in the 75, and no caller obligation is hidden: every lock precondition is established by the function that takes the hold.

residuals.description: No Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows), ASan, TSan or dudect run. The change adds pointer checks and one item-resolution helper around synchronous callbacks; no new aliasing model is claimed.

The dispatcher can check that the row declares a non-NULL item, not that the item is the type the i2r body casts the value to. A C caller may copy a public row, change its `it` slot and register the copy with the unsafe X509V3_EXT_add while keeping this callback; the callback would then read a value of another type. The row pairing is the registrar's ABI obligation, stated in every contract and not mechanically checked.
`out` must be a live BIO; the prologue establishes non-NULL only. Liveness is X509V3_EXT_print's caller obligation.
The decoded value is exclusively the dispatcher's and is released once at :372. The contracts forbid the callback from freeing, retaining or replacing it; all 22 bodies retain nothing.
A NULL `out` or `ext` is refused with 0 before the first dereference; the authority would fault. Observable return value for the non-NULL paths is unchanged.

The row's ASN.1 item is resolved once and the same pointer is used for decode and release. The authority expands ASN1_ITEM_ptr(method->it) twice; for the crate's own rows the values are identical, and for a caller-registered unstable accessor the candidate avoids a type-confused release.
A row whose item accessor answers NULL takes the failed-decode path without the authority's ASN1_item_d2i error-queue entry (TASN_DEC_140). The tested return values match.

The NULL-item guard is canaried on a live stack row, not end-to-end: a dynamic row can now be registered safely under the registry lock, but no row whose item accessor answers NULL is installed end-to-end.
The other 53 X509_VERIFY_POLICY sites are untouched and remain BLOCKED: i2s 11, v2i 10, s2i 9, i2v 7, r2i 6, print 4, audit 2, bitst 2, non-method 2. No contract or guard is claimed for them.

CLOSED by mechanism. The row resolved by X509V3_EXT_get stays live and unmodified for the whole X509V3_EXT_print call because the print holds the extension registry's read hold (RegistryReadGuard, src/x509/v3_prn.rs:271-273) across the lookup (:283), every row read (:322-331), the i2r call (:358) and the release (:372). Every writer (X509V3_EXT_add/_add_list/_add_alias/_cleanup) takes the write hold (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:613,631,661,788); the list's lazy sort moved into ext_add_locked (:565-596) so lookup is read-only. A DYNAMIC alias row cannot be released while a print is using it, demonstrated by B49-C3. The raw X509V3_EXT_get[_nid] ABI still returns a borrowed row: an external caller that keeps using that pointer across its own X509V3_EXT_cleanup remains responsible for excluding that call, which the C ABI cannot enforce.

The candidate adds synchronisation the authority does not have. EXT_LIST is now guarded by one CRYPTO_RWLOCK created by a CRYPTO_THREAD_run_once on first registry use; the block is process-lifetime (X509V3_EXT_cleanup does not free it, and must not, because the registry is reusable). Consequence for valid calls: return values and printed bytes are unchanged; the read hold is shared by readers and only writers exclude. Consequence for observability and re-entrancy: an allocator hook sees one additional CRYPTO_RWLOCK allocation (the authority makes none here); if that allocation fails, the entry points fail closed (print answers 0, lookup NULL, add 0) where the authority had no such failure; and a caller-registered i2s/i2v/i2r callback that itself calls a registry writer blocks until the print returns, where the authority would instead free the in-use row (B49-C3 cannot observe a callback that deadlocks). Both consequences are documented, not silent.
